elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Revised 11.1: "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide transition assistance..."; 11.2 now runs "Within thirty days after expiry or termination or Customer's request", so both assistance and return are anchored to expiry or termination.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: 11.1: "provide transition assistance for up to six months" — the request condition is not limited to anticipated expiry; it applies on any expiry or termination.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 11.2 as amended: "Within thirty days after expiry or termination or Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data" — the 30-day clock is now expressly anchored to expiry/termination, not only to a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Retained 11.2 language: "in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use."

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Retained 11.3: deletion occurs "After Customer confirms successful return" and "An authorized officer shall certify deletion in writing" — certification follows return as required.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same operative anchors in revised 11.1 and 11.2 ("On expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form" / "after expiry or termination").

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: 11.1 offers assistance for up to six months, which exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 11.2: return of all Customer Data in machine-readable format "Within thirty days after expiry or termination".

reasons: All six preferred elements are met in operative text: 11.1 supplies the expiry/termination trigger, the six-month cap and then-current rates; amended 11.2 supplies the 30-day return anchored to expiry or termination in a commonly used, documented machine-readable format; retained 11.3 supplies officer-certified deletion sequenced after Customer confirms successful return.

The deleted 11.1 (immediate discontinuation of all assistance and permanent deletion with no export) was walk-away language and directly contradicted 11.2/11.3; its removal is necessary to reach the checklist rather than cosmetic, and no Customer-favourable words were stripped.

Favourable existing language is retained intact — the no-withholding-for-fee-dispute sentence, metadata/relationships requirement, backup-cycle and Applicable-Law retention carve-out, and the protected-use restriction on retained copies all survive unchanged; the original request trigger in 11.2 is preserved alongside the new termination anchor rather than replaced.

No extras were added: no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no new procedures or damages categories. The phrase "or any Order Form" tracks the contract's existing Order Form structure (referenced in the Applicable Law definition) and keeps the trigger coherent with partial terminations rather than imposing an off-checklist requirement.

Intent is preserved: 11.3's "After Customer confirms successful return" still refers to a live return obligation in 11.2, no cross-reference is left dangling, no undefined term is introduced, and the retained deletion/retention mechanics no longer conflict with an immediate-deletion sentence.
